title: RELEASE_CANDIDATE_V1
description: What a version of the product must be before the Command Center may treat it as deployable. Command Center defines what is deployable: a candidate that cannot establish every identity below is refused at admission rather than completed, guessed or repaired here.

candidate_id.description: Stable name for this candidate. It exists so CANARY, DEPLOY and ROLLBACK can all name the same thing; it is not an authority.

source_repository.description: The only repository a candidate may come from. A branch name is never accepted in place of an immutable commit.

source_commit.description: An immutable commit, and specifically a commit the controlled TEST_PR channel can resolve: a PR head, not an intermediate commit of a branch.

application_tree.description: The git tree of application/ at source_commit.

source_fingerprint.description: The application source fingerprint at source_commit, computed by the repository's own definition. This entry treats it as a fixed identity and never reinterprets it.

migration_head.description: The Alembic head the candidate expects. Always stated, so the absence of a migration is a declaration rather than a missing field.

migration_required.description: Whether deploying this candidate runs a migration. The live deploy contract forbids migration, so this is false for every candidate V1 can support; it is stated explicitly so that a candidate needing one is refused here rather than discovered by the executor.

build_definition.description: How the artifact was built. The artifact is only trustworthy because this is the controlled builder's own definition and not something the caller chose.

dockerfile.description: The Dockerfile basename, never a path: the caller may not point the builder at an arbitrary file.

executor_version.description: Which builder produced this artifact. This is a statement about how the image was made, so it must be the version the signed TEST_PR Evidence itself reports for that artifact; a version outside the recognised list, or one the signed result does not corroborate, is refused rather than repaired.

artifact_digest.description: The immutable image the build produced. It must equal the artifact the signed TEST_PR result reported, or the source and the artifact are not the same claim.

required_services.description: The services this candidate needs. The enum is the live fixed eight-service topology: a candidate cannot introduce a service, and a subset is not deployable because the deploy contract requires exactly this set in this order.

test_result_identity.description: Which signed TEST_PR proves this candidate was built and tested. It is what stops 'tested commit A, deploying artifact B'.

evidence_id.description: The evidence's own identity on the evidence repository (its commit or record id).

artifact_package.description: Whether the artifact this candidate was built as still exists as a sealed, deliverable package. Optional, because a candidate written before the sealed-artifact store existed stays readable; its absence is reported as NOT_PROVEN, never assumed to be PROVEN. An image ID proves a build; it does not prove the built bytes still exist, and reading the first as the second is the ephemeral-artifact defect.

package_sha256.description: The content address of the sealed package (contract go.sealed-artifact.v1). It must be the address the signed TEST_PR result reported, and that result must be about the candidate artifact_digest.

rollback_relation.description: How this candidate relates to what is running now. V1 needs only enough to name the target a rollback would return to; full Rollback Eligibility is #104 and is deliberately not implemented here.

x-go-refusals.note: The closed set of reasons admission refuses a candidate. Tokens are reused from the live deploy contract wherever one already means the same thing, so this component adds vocabulary only where the existing words cannot express the refusal.

x-go-verdicts.note: ACCEPT means the candidate establishes every identity and nothing conflicts. REJECT means a rule above refuses it. UNKNOWN means an input the decision needs was not supplied, which is never rounded up to ACCEPT.

x-go-authority.note: Admission is a read-only decision about an identity. It creates, signs and publishes nothing.
